name: Javier Milei
summary: Austrian-school economist who calls himself an anarcho-capitalist in theory and a minarchist in practice. His government pursues deep spending cuts, deregulation, privatization and free trade. Socially he opposes abortion and what he calls 'woke' and 'gender ideology', and he is sceptical of climate policy and international organizations.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Proposed abolishing the Health ministry, privatizing public health providers and restricting free care for foreigners; his government scaled back federal health involvement.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: No direct statement found; inferred from his rejection of labour-market regulation and his labour-liberalization reforms.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Says market failures exist only in economists' models and that socialism generates only poverty.

public-ownership.rationale: Supports privatizing state companies including YPF; his Ley Bases reformed state-owned enterprises.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Calls the state the greatest enemy of wealth and Argentina a 'tax hell'; reports cutting the tax burden by about 15 points of GDP.

unions-good.rationale: Called the constitutional guarantee of labour rights 'the country's cancer'; his labour reforms were opposed by CGT general strikes.

property-fundamental.rationale: Grounds his politics in the rights to life, liberty and property and the non-aggression principle.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Deregulation is central to his programme (Decree 70/2023); he denies that market failures exist outside models.

cut-welfare.rationale: Cut subsidies and social programmes, but says he removed intermediaries so direct recipients get more; no explicit 'dependency' framing found.

worker-ownership.rationale: Implied by his wholesale rejection of socialism and defence of private enterprise.

surveillance-ok.rationale: No reliable evidence of his position found in the sources consulted.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Says drug legalization fits a free society and backs 'freedom of choice', but voted against a cannabis law and calls drug use gradual suicide.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Argues woke ideology exists to silence criticism and dissent; his government moved to remove 'femicide' from the penal code.

strong-leader.rationale: No stated endorsement, but he has governed heavily by decree, including appointing Supreme Court justices by decree.

state-harmful.rationale: 'Strictly speaking, I am an anarcho-capitalist. I despise the state'; in practice he calls himself a minarchist.

limit-guns.rationale: Supports civilian gun ownership and deregulating the legal weapons market.

empower-police-military.rationale: Cracked down on protest roadblocks, put immigration under the Security Ministry, praised Bukele's security model and sought NATO partner status.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: No statement found; not inferred from his general libertarianism.

decide-locally.rationale: No reliable evidence of his position found in the sources consulted.

rehabilitation.rationale: No reliable evidence of his position found in the sources consulted.

traditional-family.rationale: Opposes abortion and 'gender ideology', but is indifferent to same-sex marriage and treats marriage as a private contract; mixed signals.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Says he is indifferent, sees marriage as a contract, and respects any consensual relationship.

abortion-legal.rationale: Opposes abortion even in cases of rape, says life begins at conception, and wants a referendum to repeal the 2020 law.

more-religion-public.rationale: Personally religious (studies the Torah) but no stated policy view on religion's public role found.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Calls social justice 'nothing more than the disguise of socialism' and favours only equality before the law.

gender-social-construct.rationale: Calls 'gender ideology' child abuse in its extreme forms and banned gender-affirming care for minors, though he says he doesn't care about adults' gender identity.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Defends Western Greco-Roman and Judeo-Christian culture and says non-assimilating immigration becomes 'invasion'.

gradual-change.rationale: Favours 'shock' adjustment and radical cuts to the state, though he sequences reforms ('we are not liberal fools').

reduce-immigration.rationale: Tightened citizenship rules by decree, said immigrants bring 'chaos and abuse', and lists immigration among woke 'heads of the monster'.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Withdrew Argentina from the WHO, rejects the UN 2030 Agenda and says woke ideology has colonised supranational bodies.

free-trade.rationale: Eliminated import taxes and pursued trade deals, including with the EU.

nation-first.rationale: Framed the WHO exit as defending national sovereignty, while also seeking close alignment with the US, Israel and NATO.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Backs Israel's military actions and Ukraine's defence, but no statement on humanitarian intervention as such.

open-borders.rationale: His record tightens immigration and citizenship rules, despite libertarian theory.

limit-growth.rationale: Attacks 'the environmental agenda, which sets man against nature' as a pretext for taxation.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Lists climate change among woke 'heads of the same monster' and has criticised and weighed leaving the Paris Agreement.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: No reliable evidence of his position found in the sources consulted.

experts-over-public.rationale: No reliable evidence of his position found in the sources consulted.

central-planning.rationale: Says socialism generates only poverty and market failures don't exist.

socialized-markets.rationale: Privatizes state firms and rejects socialism in all forms.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Rejects state economic steering, dropped an EV battery bid and wants to shut or redefine CONICET.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Implied by his defence of free-enterprise capitalism.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: Favours 'currency competition and eliminating the central bank', calling it one of the greatest thieves in history.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: His labour liberalization dismantles state-backed sectoral rules, and he rejects the Peronist labour model.

one-party-rule.rationale: Describes the system he defends as a republican liberal democracy with checks and balances.

democracy-best.rationale: Endorses republican liberal democracy, but his ideal is anarcho-capitalist and his record includes governing by decree.

workers-councils.rationale: Implied by his anti-socialism and support for liberal democracy.

restore-past-order.rationale: Holds up 1860s 'pure liberalism' as Argentina's lost model, but that is liberal rather than traditionalist.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Openly ideological yet pragmatic in sequencing reforms; no clear position.

notes: Born 22 October 1970; living and serving as president as of the audit date. He distinguishes his anarcho-capitalist ideal from his minarchist practice; answers follow his practice where they differ, except where a statement asks about the ideal itself. Many social and institutional statements have no recorded position in the sources consulted and are left null rather than inferred from his ideology.
